questions.question: In OR Modelling, which description defines a network?
options: A set of vertices in which every pair of vertices is joined directly by an edge
A set of vertices that each carry a number, such as a cost or a capacity
A set of vertices with edges, each edge joining a specified pair of vertices
A map that shows locations and roads at their true positions and lengths

questions.question: Which statement about edge directions and numerical edge values in a network is correct?
options: Each is added only when the problem being modelled needs it
Every edge needs a value; a network without numbers is not a model
Edges may carry values only if they also carry directions
Values are optional, but every edge must have a direction

questions.question: Network $N_R$ models six towns joined by roads; network $N_K$ models six computers joined by cables. Both use vertex labels $1,\dots,6$, join the same pairs and carry the same edge values. How do $N_R$ and $N_K$ compare as networks?
options: They differ, since roads and cables are different objects
They differ, since cables must be given directions
They agree only if the towns lie as far apart as the computers
They are the same network; only the interpretation differs

questions.question: Between depots $X$ and $Y$ there is no road. In a network whose edge values are driving costs, a student enters an edge $X\text{-}Y$ with value 0 so that no pair of depots is left out. What is wrong with this?
options: Nothing is wrong: no road and a road at cost 0 are the same thing
An edge with value 0 is a free road; no road means no edge at all
The value should be the straight-line distance between $X$ and $Y$
Every pair does need an edge, but its value must be positive

questions.question: A bakery $O$ supplies shops $S_1,S_2,S_3$ along the roads $O\text{-}S_1$, $O\text{-}S_2$ and $S_2\text{-}S_3$. In a network model of these roads, what are the vertices and the edges?
options: Vertices $O,S_1,S_2,S_3$; edges the three roads
Vertices the three roads; edges the four sites
Vertices $S_1,S_2,S_3$ only; edges the three roads
Vertices $O,S_1,S_2,S_3$; edges all six pairs of sites

questions.question: In a water network, the pipe between pumping stations $U$ and $W$ has edge value 40, and the edge values are capacities in litres per second. What does the value 40 state?
options: The pipe between stations $U$ and $W$ is 40 metres long
Exactly 40 litres per second flow through this pipe
Station $U$ can store up to 40 litres of water at a time
At most 40 litres per second can pass through the pipe

questions.question: Lorries may drive from depot $P$ to depot $Q$ along a one-way road, but not from $Q$ to $P$. How should a network represent this road?
options: As an edge between $P$ and $Q$ that carries no direction at all
As an edge between $P$ and $Q$ with direction from $P$ to $Q$
As two edges, one from $P$ to $Q$ and one from $Q$ to $P$
By leaving the road out, since it cannot be used both ways

questions.question: A network is described by the vertex set $V=\{1,2,3,4\}$ and the edges $1\text{-}2$, $2\text{-}3$ and $3\text{-}5$. What is wrong with this description?
options: No edge has an end at vertex $4$, which is not allowed
Edge $3\text{-}5$ ends at 5, which is not a vertex in $V$
The edges carry no values, so the description is unfinished
Four vertices in $V$ need at least four edges between them

questions.question: A distribution model needs two numbers: the toll on each road between two depots, and the storage space of each depot. Which of these is suited to be an edge value in the depot network?
options: The storage space, since it describes where goods can be kept
Both, since every number in a model becomes an edge value
The toll, since it belongs to a road joining two depots
Neither, since edge values can only be distances in km

questions.question: A network has vertices $A,B,C,D$ and edges $A\text{-}B$, $B\text{-}C$, $C\text{-}D$, with no directions and no edge values. Which question can be answered from this network alone?
options: How many kilometres the connection $A\text{-}B$ is long
Whether vertex $D$ lies north or south of vertex $B$
Whether vertex $A$ and vertex $C$ are joined by an edge
How much it costs to build the connection $C\text{-}D$

questions.question: A road runs from town $A$ to town $B$ through village $M$, and at $M$ a road to town $C$ branches off. With the towns and $M$ as vertices, which edge set models these roads?
options: $A\text{-}B$ and $M\text{-}C$
$A\text{-}M$, $M\text{-}B$ and $M\text{-}C$
$A\text{-}B$, $A\text{-}C$ and $B\text{-}C$
$A\text{-}M$, $M\text{-}B$ and $A\text{-}C$

questions.question: Six stations are numbered $1,\dots,6$. A direct link joins stations $i$ and $j$ exactly when $|i-j|=1$ or $|i-j|=3$. How many edges does the station network have?
options: 8 edges: 5 with difference 1 and 3 with difference 3
5 edges, one for each pair of neighbouring stations
16 edges, listing $i\text{-}j$ and $j\text{-}i$ separately
9 edges: 5 with difference 1 and 4 with difference 3

questions.question: Road $A\text{-}B$ crosses road $C\text{-}D$ on a bridge, with no way to switch roads; in the drawing of the network the two edges cross. Should the crossing point become a vertex?
options: Yes; every point where two drawn edges cross becomes a vertex
No; the roads are not connected there, so no vertex is added
Yes, but only if the two roads have equal edge values
No, because a network drawing must avoid crossing edges

questions.question: Network $N_1$ on vertices $A,B,C,D$ has edges $A\text{-}B$ (value 3), $B\text{-}C$ (value 5) and $C\text{-}D$ (value 2). A student claims that any network on $A,B,C,D$ with three edges valued 3, 5 and 2 equals $N_1$. Which network refutes the claim?
options: $N_1$ with its three edges and values listed in reverse order
$N_1$ redrawn on paper with vertex $D$ placed far from $C$
$N_1$ with a fourth edge $A\text{-}D$ of value 7 added
$N_1$ with edge $B\text{-}C$ replaced by $B\text{-}D$, also of value 5

questions.question: Pipes $U\text{-}V$ and $V\text{-}W$ have edge values 5 and 3, which are capacities in litres per second, and station $V$ only passes water on. A student adds the values: 8 litres per second can go from $U$ to $W$ via $V$. Which conclusion is correct?
options: At most 8 per second, since edge values add along a route
At most 5 per second, the capacity of the first pipe
At most 4 per second, the average of the two capacities
At most 3 per second, since each litre passes both pipes
